title: Embedding-Space Toxicity Direction: Does Attenuating It Preserve or Destroy Capability?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: if embedding-space toxicity attenuation preserves capability while bypassing alignment, it is a practical attack tool. However, the safety contribution is characterizing an attack rather than building a defense, which weakens the impact chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Implementing ETTA-style linear transformations on embeddings, evaluating on multiple benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, coding), and comparing against activation steering requires advanced ML understanding and significant compute for evaluation.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The interpolation experiment is reasonably scoped, but evaluation on three different benchmarks plus StrongREJECT plus comparison with activation steering expands scope. Sustained effort needed.

novelty.reasoning: This idea has been directly addressed by ETTA (Embedding Transformation Toxicity Attenuation), published as arXiv:2507.08020 and under review. ETTA identifies and attenuates toxicity-sensitive dimensions in embedding space via linear transformations, achieves 88.61% ASR on AdvBench across 5 open-source LLMs, and reports minimal capability degradation (5.63% drop on TruthfulQA, 7.77% on MMLU). The proposed research -- testing whether embedding-space toxicity attenuation preserves capability -- has been comprehensively answered by ETTA with the exact same methodology (linear transformations on embeddings, multi-benchmark capability evaluation). The proposed idea is essentially a replication of existing work.
